newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Cargo must break even - Weber.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo must break even - Weber.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo is under strong pressure to break even this year, Deutsche Lufthansa AG chairman Juergen Weber said.
Weber told a Frankfurt news conference he wanted to see the cargo unit leave the loss zone this year after it plunged into the red last year.
Lufthansa Cargo made a loss of 59.8 million marks on a turnover of 3.4 billion marks in 1996, largely prompted by a weak market, falling yields and higher fuel costs.
Weber described the figure of an expected 1997 pre-tax loss of 40 million marks disclosed by Lufthansa Cargo chairman Wilhelm Althen last November as "a plan figure".
"The 30 million mark improvement in the first quarter gives hope that we are not too far away from my hope," he said.
Lufthansa Cargo cut its first quarter loss to 10 million marks in 1997 from a 40 million mark loss in the same period last year.
Weber added: "Freight has improved in 1997. There is a movement in the right direction but the major improvements from the measures will come first in 1998."
He described the 800 milion marks paid by Lufthansa Cargo AG to Deutsche Lufthansa AG for the purchase of the entire belly cargo capacity of Lufthansa passenger aircraft as "a fair price".
The purchase price was calculated on the basis of market rates and production costs, he added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
